maria: Heads up — ran the nightly quantized eval for the new 16k HF snapshot and seeing a subtle quality regression vs float32. metrics dropped on long-dialog SQuAD-style prompts.
kevin: regression where exactly? tokenization? kernel?
mar ia: looks like token bleed around system role boundaries in chat templates. It only shows up when we enable `sliding_window` and use `rope_scaling` != 1.0.
sam: can you paste the config.json fragment?
maria: sure — snippet:```json
{"model_type": "causal", "max_position_embeddings": 16384, "rope_scaling": {"type": "linear", "factor": 1.05}, "sliding_window": true, "num_key_value_heads": 32}```
kevin: num_key_value_heads=32 is the HF count, but our serving runtime expects kv heads to be divisor-aligned with present head mapping. Did conversion warn?
maria: hf-convert printed a warning about `kv_head_mismatch` but the converter proceeded. I thought the chat template shim would handle special tokens.
anita: quick note: our tokenizers strip some soft-special tokens in the shim. If sliding_window moves the span, special token indices shift and can change KV cache indexing for attention — explains bleed.
sam: is this only in quantized runs?
maria: interestingly yes — float32 baseline doesn't show the regression. Quant (int8 + per-channel) amplifies tiny attention misalignments into measurable F1 drops.
kevin: possible mismatch between HF attention layout and our optimized kernels when `rope_scaling` != 1.0. Kernel assumes original rotary angles; scaling modifies sin/cos coords. If kv head mapping is off by 1, the rotation mixes heads.
anita: steps: 1) re-run converter with strict kv head check (`--fail-on-kv-mismatch`), 2) compare token ids for role/user/system tokens after chat shim, 3) run small single-step debug with `UNROLL=1` to dump kv shapes.
maria: ran step 1 — converter now fails (good). Example error: `Mismatch: expected num_kv_heads=32, model reported 40`
sam: 32 vs 40 — that's not a tiny off-by-one. Could be tokenizer adding pseudo-tokens?
kevin: sometimes HF export packs shared Q/K dims differently for multiquery setups. Are we sure this model isn't using grouped-kv?
anita: checked — model config `architectures` includes `GroupedQueryAttention` in the HF repo notes. That maps to different `num_key_value_heads` semantics. Converter mis-translated grouped-kv -> plain kv heads count.
maria: so combination of grouped-kv conversion bug + chat shim moving special token indices + rope scaling change = perfect storm that only surfaces under quant.
sam: action items?
kevin: (1) Add grouped-kv detection in converter and preserve `group_size` metadata; (2) Harden chat shim to keep absolute special token offsets (no silent trimming); (3) Add an automated quant smoke that compares token sequences and kv shapes between HF loader and Redwood runtime before large evals.
anita: I'll open a small PR for the chat shim fix.
maria: I'm starting the quant-smoke with `--compare-tokens --dump-kv` now. command:```bash
python tools/quant_smoke.py --model ./converted --hf-src ./hf --dump-kv --out /tmp/kv-diffs.log```
deploy-bot: CI: build queued for branch fix/chat-shim-specials (#1289) :building_construction:
kevin: thanks — moving to triage board. If we block conversion, roll out fallback: force `rope_scaling` = 1.0 and disable `sliding_window` for the affected commit so hosted doesn't get bad regressions.
maria: noted. Will paste the kv-diffs when done.
sam: thx — good catch, this was slipping past evals because we only compared perplexity earlier not long-dialog F1.
anita: will also add unit that mutates rope scaling by 0.01 and checks attention stability in quantized kernels.
maria: ideal — that should catch this earlier.
kevin: summary: grouped-kv conversion + chat-template special-token shift + rope scaling produce quantized attention head misalignment. Patch converter, shim, and add quant-smoke.
maria: pinging @eng-ml to watch the next nightly. :eyes:
